company_name: Templeton Emerging Markets Investment Trust plc (TEMIT)
fx_note: Statements, NAV and dividends are GBP (pence/share); TEM.NZ quotes NZD on the NZX. GBPNZD 2.3016 (Yahoo GBPNZD=X, 2026-09-03T10:25Z). Parity check against the London primary line: TEM.L 319.0p x 2.3016 / 100 = NZ$7.3421 vs TEM.NZ NZ$7.386 -- NZX line is 0.60% above parity, i.e. the two lines are consistent. Parent brief quoted 2.3014 (0.01% apart). All values computed in pence first; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are NZD so they compare to current_price.

valuation_philosophy.model: NAV per share compounding + exit discount to NAV, discounted at a GBP cost of equity (same family as AFI.NZ, MLN.NZ, BIT.NZ, BIF.NZ).
valuation_philosophy.why_no_dcf: TEMIT is a UK closed-end investment trust holding ~GBP3.2bn of listed emerging-markets equities. It has no operating cash flow: 'revenue' (GBP65.6m FY2026) is portfolio dividend income and reported net income (GBP758.5m FY2026, -GBP442.4m FY2022) is mark-to-market capital return. Discounting either at a WACC is meaningless; EPS (77.54p FY2026, 0.22p FY2023, -37.46p FY2022) is noise, so P/E is not computed. The market-clearing metric for a trust is price/NAV, so the model projects NAV/share and applies an exit P/NAV anchored in the trust's own 11-year discount history.
valuation_philosophy.mechanics: NAV_t = NAV_(t-1) x (1 + gross portfolio return - ongoing charges + buyback accretion) - dividend paid. Dividends leave the NAV and are added back as cash to the holder in the same year (modelled once, not twice). Exit value = year-5 NAV x (1 - exit discount). IV = PV(dividends) + PV(exit value) at the cost of equity. NAV is already an equity figure net of the RCF, so net debt is NOT subtracted.
valuation_philosophy.fx_chain: A NZ holder carries three currency layers: (1) EM local currencies (TWD, KRW, CNY/HKD, BRL, INR, MXN...) inside the GBP NAV -- unhedged; (2) GBP itself, since NAV and dividends are GBP; (3) GBP/NZD on the NZX quote. The valuation is done in pence and translated at spot, so the NZD IV moves 1:1 with GBP/NZD independent of anything the trust does. GBPNZD ranged 2.28-2.31 over the past three months alone.
valuation_philosophy.anchor_note: Anchored on the published cum-income NAV of 351.03p at 1-Sep-2026 (NZX daily NAV announcement 479076, unaudited), not the audited 31-Mar-2026 NAV of 267.3p. NAV rose 31% between March and September (EM rally; EEM +23% in USD, GBPUSD +2%), so using the March NAV against a September price would have shown a spurious ~19% premium; against the current NAV the London line is at a 9.1% discount.

inputs.notes: MODEL: NAV/NTA + exit-discount (dcf-methods routing row 'LIC, investment trust, closed-end fund'). Reason: closed-end trust holding listed EM equities -- no operating cash flow, income statement is mark-to-market. An owner-FCF DCF would discount portfolio dividend income at a WACC and subtract an RCF that NAV already nets, producing a meaningless number. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). DATA QUIRKS: (1) Metrics.csv NAVPerShare/SharesOutstanding/EPS for FY2017-FY2020 are PRE the 5-for-1 sub-division of 26-Jul-2021 (763p FY2017 = 152.6p split-adjusted); FY2021+ are post-split. (2) Analysis JSON's '10-yr benchmark 89.3%' is the OUTPERFORMANCE margin -- the FY2026 highlights table gives MSCI EM 10-yr cumulative +131.0%, 5-yr +25.4%, 3-yr +42.0%. (3) The analysis JSON labels the six months to 30-Sep-2025 'H1 FY2027'; it is H1 FY2026.

historical_growth.methodology: Growth driver is NAV per share TOTAL RETURN (cum-income, dividends reinvested), the trust's own KPI, against MSCI EM (net dividends, GBP). Revenue/EPS/equity CAGRs shown for schema completeness only: revenue is portfolio dividend income, EPS is mark-to-market, and total equity is distorted by GBP600m+ of buybacks over five years.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: nav_total_return_5yr_cagr_pct -- the sober through-cycle figure; FY2026's +41.3% and the 3-yr 18.3% are a single exceptional year and are NOT extrapolated
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.5% 5-yr) diverges from NAV-per-share growth (+4.0% 5-yr) by design: GBP600m+ of buybacks shrank total equity while lifting per-share NAV. Not a data error; per-share NAV is the driver.
historical_growth.notes: FY2026 (+41.3% vs +26.8%) was driven by the AI/semiconductor overweight (TSMC, SK Hynix, Samsung, MediaTek ~33% of NAV). FY2022 (-17.3%) shows the drawdown side. The 5-yr NAV TR of 6.7%/yr spans both.

assumption_rationale.base: Gross 8.5%/yr = ~7.5% through-cycle EM equity return in GBP (10-yr MSCI EM 8.7%/yr includes the FY2026 boom; 5-yr 4.6%) plus 1.0pp of manager alpha, a haircut on the 2.1-3.6pp/yr delivered over 5-10 years. Net of the new ~0.71% OCR and 0.2-0.4%/yr buyback accretion (GBP300m programme front-loaded, history 0.0-1.2%/yr) this is an 8.1% net NAV total return -- between the 5-yr record (6.7%) and the 10-yr (12.3%), nearer the sober end. Dividend 1.5% of NAV (5.25p/351p), floor 5.00p. Exit discount 10.0%: current 9.1%, held roughly flat with a slight drift toward the 10-yr average of 11.3% (range 7.7-15.4%). No further narrowing assumed -- 8-9% is the narrow end of TEMIT's own history and FY2026's re-rating does not repeat. Cost of equity 11.0% = UK 10-yr gilt ~4.5% (Sep-2026, estimate) + 5.0% global ERP + 1.5% EM beta/country premium; GBP-based because the flows are GBP.
assumption_rationale.bull: Gross 12.0%/yr matches the 10-yr NAV TR record (12.3%/yr) -- EM re-rates vs stretched US mega-caps and the AI/semiconductor cycle persists. OCR falls toward 0.65% as NAV grows into the 0.5% fee band. Exit discount 5.0%: narrower than any year-end print in 11 years (7.7% best, FY2021) but supported by the GBP300m buyback, the tender-offer floor at NAV-2% and peer re-ratings on sustained outperformance. Deliberately outside the observed range; weighted 25%.
assumption_rationale.bear: Year-1 -12% NAV drawdown (FY2022 was -17.3%) as the AI/semis theme that drove FY2026 reverses, then 4-6%/yr (5-yr benchmark 4.6%/yr, no alpha) -- a ~1.7%/yr gross 5-yr CAGR, i.e. the 2011-2020 EM 'lost decade' pattern. OCR 0.76% (smaller NAV, more in the 1% band). Buyback accretion higher (0.3-0.5%) because a wider discount makes each pound more accretive. Dividend held at the 5.00p floor. Exit discount 15.0% = FY2024 wide (15.4%).
assumption_rationale.weights: 25/50/25. No solvency or refinancing risk (1.2% gearing, liquid listed portfolio) so the bear is a market/discount drawdown, not impairment; the bull is capped by an exit discount already near the narrow end of history. Symmetric weights match the LIC precedents (AFI.NZ, MLN.NZ, BIT.NZ).

static_cross_check.description: Current NAV x (1 - scenario exit discount): what the trust is worth TODAY at the scenario's fair discount, ignoring the 5-year build. The 5-year IV falls below this when the expected net NAV return (8.1% base) is below the 11% cost of equity -- the gap is the return cushion the model demands, not a discount assumption.

entry_price.methodology: Price today at which 5 years of scenario dividends plus the year-5 exit value (year-5 NAV x (1 - exit discount)), all discounted at 15%, equal that price. The exit value is an explicit P/NAV judgement, not a Gordon terminal value, so there is no growth-rate/discount-rate term to rebuild at the hurdle -- the same exit value is discounted at 15% instead of 11%. Self-consistency: the 15% row of required_return_table equals the base entry price and the 11% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value.
entry_price.memo: A 15% hurdle on an asset whose base-case net return is ~8.1%/yr requires buying at -33% to NAV -- deeper than TEMIT has traded in 11 years (widest year-end 15.4%). As with AFI.NZ and BIT.NZ this is the correct output, not a target: an EM equity trust cannot organically deliver 15% from any price it has historically reached. Judge it against its ~11% cost of equity instead.

required_return_table.note: Each row re-discounts the same base dividends and exit value at that rate. 11% row = valuation.base.intrinsic_value; 15% row = entry_price.base.

sensitivity.note: Two grids, both base-case flows, GBP pence and NZD (at 2.3016). Grid 1 varies cost of equity x exit discount; grid 2 varies gross portfolio return x exit discount at 11% CoE.

probability_weighted.weighted_iv_currency_note: weighted_iv is NZD to match the TEM.NZ quote currency (screener canonical); weighted_iv_gbp_pence is the native London figure.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street SBC band collapsed: no SBC exists, so house = street and band_position is null.

sanity_check.description: Investment-trust sanity anchor is price-to-NAV, not P/E or EV/EBITDA. P/E: not applicable -- EPS is mark-to-market (77.54p FY2026, 0.22p FY2023, -37.46p FY2022). EV/EBITDA: not applicable -- no EBITDA concept for a securities portfolio and net debt is inside NAV. A future reader should NOT 'fix' these nulls. Check: each scenario's exit P/NAV against TEMIT's own 11-year year-end discount range (7.7% to 15.4%, FY2016-FY2026).
observations: Base exit discount 10.0% and bear 15.0% sit inside the observed range; bull 5.0% is deliberately 2.7pp narrower than the best year-end print (7.7%, FY2021) -- a stretch justified only by the tender-offer floor and the GBP300m buyback, and weighted 25%.

The IV-implied P/NAV today (base 0.80x) is below the historical range because the model discounts an ~8.1% expected return at an 11% cost of equity; it is not a discount assumption. At a discount rate equal to the expected return the value converges on NAV x 0.90 (see static_cross_check and required_return_table).
Current price/NAV 0.909x (discount 9.1%) is between the base (10%) and bull (5%) exit assumptions: the market is already paying roughly the base-case fair discount for today's NAV.

key_risks_to_valuation: Three-layer FX chain: EM local currencies inside the GBP NAV, GBP itself, and GBP/NZD on the NZX quote. A 5% GBP/NZD move is a 5% NZD IV move with no change in the trust.
Concentration: TSMC + SK Hynix + Samsung + MediaTek ~33% of NAV; ~46% China/HK + Taiwan. FY2026's alpha and the March-September NAV surge came from this theme.
Discount volatility: FY2024 15.4% to FY2026 8.2% in two years; the Board itself calls the historic discount 'unsatisfactory' and does not believe buybacks alone close it.

The daily NAV anchor is unaudited and moves ~1%/day; the 1-Sep-2026 figure will be stale within weeks. Refresh nav_per_share_pence from the NZX 'Net Asset Value(s)' feed before relying on the upside figure.
NZX line liquidity: thin, can diverge from London parity; the 0.6% premium at valuation date is within normal noise.
